items.review_rationale: Reviewed natural numbers as positive counting sequence 1,2,3,... contrasted with N_{>0} notation when another convention includes zero.

references.phrase: zero-inclusive natural numbers N as contrast

references.context: Counting numbers starting at one and omitting zero.
Notation for strictly positive natural numbers under zero-inclusive convention.

references.disposition: The primary meaning of N in this formulation starts at one; no claim that zero belongs to it.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed equivalence relation as subset of SxS with reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity, preserving quantified logical implications and set of ordered pairs.

references.context: Collection of ordered pairs of elements of S, represented by a subset of Cartesian square.
Every element x of S is related to itself.
Relation holds in reverse order whenever it holds forward.

references.phrase: transitivity x~y and y~z imply x~z
references.context: Two consecutive related pairs yield related outer endpoints.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed quotient set of equivalence relation as collection of all equivalence classes [x] on underlying set S, not an arbitrary subset of S.

references.context: Collection containing exactly the distinct equivalence classes of S under relation ~.
Each class appearing in quotient has at least one representative element x of S.

references.phrase: quotient elements are classes not individual points
references.disposition: Different representatives can determine the same quotient element.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed equivalence class [x] as all y in S satisfying y~x for fixed x and an equivalence relation; all its members represent the same class.

references.phrase: subset of S represented by class

references.context: Elements y of S belonging to class exactly when they relate to chosen representative x.
Any two members of one equivalence class determine the same class under the relation.

references.disposition: The representative x is a choice of element used to describe the class, not necessarily a unique distinguished element.
